title: Eight powers impose the Boxer Protocol on China
note: An eight-nation intervention ended with an indemnity, foreign garrisons and bans on arms imports for China. Settling a war on terms the loser cannot revise is one way a defeat becomes the grievance behind the next conflict.

title: The first powered flight, at Kitty Hawk
note: A twelve second hop opened a domain that within a decade carried reconnaissance and bombs. Military organizations adopted the aircraft faster than any law of war kept up with it.

title: Japan attacks the Russian fleet at Port Arthur
note: A surprise naval attack opened a war between two empires over Korea and Manchuria, fought without a declaration first. Both sides had believed the other would concede rather than fight.

title: The first Moroccan crisis tests the new alignments
note: A German challenge to French primacy in Morocco was meant to split the new understanding between France and Britain and instead hardened it. Crises that fail to break an alignment usually deepen it.

title: The Russian fleet is destroyed in the Tsushima Strait
note: A European great power lost a fleet to an Asian one in a single battle, and the war ended within months. Defeat abroad fed revolution at home in Russia, a pattern repeated in 1917.

title: A run on a New York trust sets off the Panic of 1907
note: A banking panic with no central bank behind it was contained by private rescue, and the episode led to the creation of the Federal Reserve in 1913. Financial fragility shapes what states can afford when a war arrives.

title: An uprising at Wuchang ends the Chinese empire
note: The Qing dynasty fell and a republic that could not control its own generals took its place, opening decades of warlord rule. A weak center in a large state invites both internal war and outside intervention.

title: The Balkan League attacks the Ottoman Empire
note: Four small states won quickly and pushed Ottoman rule almost out of Europe, redrawing borders the great powers then had to bless. Each had a great power patron watching, which is how a regional war becomes everyone's problem.

title: The winners of the first Balkan war turn on each other
note: Bulgaria attacked its former allies over the division of Macedonia and lost, leaving it looking for a patron willing to reverse the result. Unsettled spoils from one war are a standing invitation to the next.

title: The Austrian heir is shot in Sarajevo
note: A regional dispute between an empire and a small neighbor, with a great-power patron behind each.

title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
note: Still a local war. Every capital expected the other side to back down.

title: Germany declares war on Russia
note: Russian mobilization for Serbia triggers the German war plan against France and Russia together. The alliances fire.

title: Germany declares war on France
note: The two-front war the German plan was built for.

title: Britain declares war on Germany
note: The conventional start date for a general European war. Four major powers are now fighting each other directly.

limitations: Death toll estimates range widely and the characterization remains politically contested.
title: Mass deportations and killings of Ottoman Armenians begin
note: Under cover of war the Ottoman government deported and killed its Armenian population, with deaths generally estimated between 600,000 and 1.5 million. Wartime emergency powers are repeatedly the setting in which states turn on their own civilians.

title: Allied troops land on the Gallipoli peninsula
note: An attempt to knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war by forcing the straits became an eight month stalemate and a withdrawal. It is the standard case of a plan to shorten a war that lengthened it.

title: The Somme offensive opens on the Western Front
note: More than a million men were killed or wounded over four and a half months for a few miles of ground. When neither side can win quickly and neither can afford to quit, the war stops being about the original dispute.

title: The United States enters the war
note: Unrestricted submarine warfare brings in the last major power still outside.

limitations: Dated by the Gregorian calendar; Russian sources of the time used 25 October.
title: The Bolsheviks take power in Petrograd
note: A great power left the war through revolution rather than defeat, freeing German divisions for the west and creating a state that other powers treated as an enemy on principle. War strain and regime collapse run in both directions.

limitations: The first recorded case is disputed; the 4 March 1918 Kansas case is a common but not certain marker. Death toll estimates range from 17 to 50 million or more.
title: The 1918 influenza pandemic reaches the armies
note: An influenza pandemic spread along troop movements and killed on the order of tens of millions worldwide, more than the war itself. Wartime censorship in the belligerent states delayed public warning almost everywhere.

limitations: Start dates for the civil war range from late 1917 to mid 1918; the May 1918 revolt is one common marker.
title: The Russian civil war becomes a general war
note: A revolt along the Trans-Siberian railway turned scattered resistance into a multi-front civil war that drew in Allied expeditionary forces. Foreign intervention in a civil war rarely decides it and reliably poisons relations afterwards.

title: Armistice
note: The name World War arrived during the fighting; the numeral came later.

title: The Treaty of Versailles is signed
note: The settlement assigned war guilt, stripped territory and set reparations that were revised repeatedly and never paid in full. A peace strong enough to humiliate but too weak to enforce is the textbook setup for revision by force.

title: The League of Nations comes into being
note: The first standing organization for collective security opened without the United States and with no force of its own. It could name an aggressor but could not stop one, which is what the 1930s tested.

title: The Ottoman Empire is partitioned at Sevres
note: The treaty carved up Ottoman territory, was rejected by the nationalist movement in Anatolia, and was replaced three years later after a war the victors had not planned for. Imposing a settlement on a government that no longer controls the country does not end anything.

title: Reparations are fixed at 132 billion gold marks
note: The reparations bill was set under threat of occupation and became the central grievance of German politics for a decade. War debts and reparations tied the economies of former enemies together in a way that transmitted every crisis.

title: The naval powers agree to limit capital ships
note: Five powers accepted tonnage ratios and a battleship holiday, the first modern arms control treaty with real cuts. It worked while the signatories wanted it to and collapsed once one of them decided the ratio was a permanent second place.

title: A fascist movement is handed power in Italy
note: A paramilitary march ended with the king inviting the fascist leadership to form a government rather than resisting it. The first fascist state in Europe supplied both a model and, later, a partner for the next one.

title: Greece and Turkey agree a compulsory population exchange
note: About 1.6 million people were moved across the Aegean by treaty, sorted by religion, after a war that had already displaced most of them. It ended the fighting and set a precedent that partitions later in the century copied.

title: German hyperinflation ends with a new currency
note: Prices had risen to the point where a single dollar bought trillions of marks before a replacement currency stopped it. The savings of the German middle class were wiped out, and the political effects outlasted the monetary fix by a decade.

title: The New York stock market crashes
note: The crash began a depression that spread through the gold standard and short term credit into every industrial economy. Mass unemployment gave the movements that wanted to overturn the 1919 settlement their opening.

title: Mass civil disobedience begins in British India
note: A 240 mile march against the salt monopoly opened a campaign that filled the prisons and made the cost of holding India visible. Anti-colonial pressure was already reshaping what the European empires could commit elsewhere.

title: The United States raises tariffs across the board
note: The tariff invited retaliation and helped world trade fall by roughly two thirds over three years. States that cannot buy what they need turn to taking it, which is the argument the expansionist powers then made at home.

title: Japan seizes Manchuria
note: Some historians date the Second World War from here. On the conventional European dating it is a prelude.

title: Britain leaves the gold standard
note: After a run on sterling Britain suspended convertibility, and much of the world followed into competing currency blocs. The blocs turned trade into a matter of empire and alignment rather than price.

limitations: Death toll estimates range from about 5 to 8 million across the affected regions.
title: Peasants are barred from leaving the famine regions
note: A directive stopped movement out of Ukraine and the North Caucasus while requisitioning continued, and several million people died in the famine of 1932 and 1933. Policy, not weather, turned a bad harvest into mass death.

title: The Nazi party takes power in Germany
note: A party committed to overturning the 1919 settlement was appointed to government and dismantled the republic within months. Rearmament and territorial revision followed as stated policy rather than as improvisation.

title: The League condemns the seizure of Manchuria and Japan leaves
note: The Assembly adopted a report finding Japan the aggressor, Japan walked out, and nothing followed. The first test of collective security showed that naming an aggressor without a cost is an invitation to the next one.

title: A dust storm darkens the southern plains
note: Drought and plowed grassland produced storms that stripped topsoil from millions of acres and pushed hundreds of thousands of people off the land. Environmental collapse inside a rich state still took a decade and a federal program to arrest.

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
note: The League of Nations fails its first serious test. Restraints on force weaken across the system.

title: German troops re-enter the Rhineland
note: A treaty limit was broken with a force too small to resist a French response, and no response came. Each unanswered move lowered the price of the next one and taught the German leadership that the guarantors were bluffing.

title: Spanish civil war begins
note: A civil war that Germany, Italy and the Soviet Union all arm. The first theater where the coming coalitions test each other.

title: Full war between Japan and China
note: Chinese historiography dates the world war from here. Two years before Poland, the deadliest theater of the war is already open.

title: Four powers hand the Sudetenland to Germany
note: Britain, France, Germany and Italy transferred Czechoslovak territory without Czechoslovakia in the room, in exchange for a promise of no further claims. The promise lasted five months, which is why the word Munich now means a concession that buys nothing.

title: Polish cryptanalysts hand Enigma decryption to Britain and France
note: Five weeks before the invasion, Polish intelligence gave its allies the reconstructed machine and its methods, which became the basis of the wartime decryption effort. Reading an enemy's traffic changes what leaders believe they know when they choose to fight.

title: Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact
note: A public non-aggression treaty carried secret protocols dividing eastern Europe into spheres, removing the two front problem that had held Germany back. War in Poland followed nine days later.

title: Germany invades Poland; Britain and France declare war two days later
note: The conventional start date. On this dating the war in Asia is folded in retrospectively.

title: Germany attacks in the west
note: France falls in six weeks. Britain fights on alone in Europe.

title: The air battle over Britain begins
note: The first campaign decided by air power alone denied Germany the conditions for invasion and kept a base in Europe for the coalition that formed later. Radar and ground control, not aircraft numbers, carried the defense.

title: Italy invades Egypt
note: The Mediterranean becomes a theater because Italy joined Germany's war.

title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
note: The largest land war in history opens. A preventive war by a leadership convinced its window was closing.

title: The United States freezes Japanese assets and cuts off oil
note: The freeze, matched by Britain and the Dutch East Indies, ended about four fifths of Japan's oil imports and set a clock running on its fleet. Sanctions meant to deter can instead narrow a target's choices to attacking sooner.

title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor; Germany declares war on the United States four days later
note: The date the Asian and European wars become one war. Every major power is now in direct combat.

title: Officials coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews
note: A meeting of ministry and police officials organized the machinery of a killing programme already under way, which took about six million lives. Genocide here was administered by a functioning bureaucracy under the cover of a war.

limitations: Casualty figures for both sides are estimates and vary between sources.
title: The battle for Stalingrad begins
note: Five months of urban and encirclement fighting cost close to two million casualties on both sides and destroyed a German army. It is the point after which the German position in the east was never restored.

limitations: Only the year is used as a date; deaths were concentrated in the second half of 1943. Toll estimates range from about 2 to 3.8 million.
title: Famine in Bengal kills millions during the war
note: A cyclone, a lost import route, wartime requisitioning and export bans between Indian provinces combined into a famine that killed roughly two to three million people. Relief was slowed by the priorities of a war being fought next door.

limitations: Scale-up ran through 1943 and 1944; the March 1944 plant opening is one marker among several.
title: Deep tank fermentation puts penicillin into mass production
note: A new fermentation process moved penicillin from laboratory quantities to millions of doses in time for the invasion of France. Wound infection stopped being the main way a wounded soldier died.

title: Allied forces land in Normandy
note: The largest amphibious operation ever mounted opened a second front in western Europe against an enemy already losing in the east. From here the war's end was a question of timing and of who would hold which capital.

title: Forty four nations design the postwar monetary system
note: Delegates agreed on fixed but adjustable exchange rates, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, explicitly to avoid repeating the currency blocs of the 1930s. The economic settlement was written before the war it followed had ended.

title: The three main allies divide postwar Europe
note: The meeting set occupation zones, the terms for a Soviet entry into the Pacific war, and the shape of governments in eastern Europe. What each side thought it had agreed differed, and that gap became the opening of the next confrontation.

title: Fifty states sign the United Nations Charter
note: The Charter banned the use of force except in self defense or when the Security Council authorizes it, and gave five powers a veto over that authorization. Making the strongest states permanent judges was the price of getting them to join.

title: The first nuclear device is detonated in New Mexico
note: A test in the desert proved a weapon that made the destruction of a city the work of one aircraft. Every later argument about deterrence, arms control and proliferation starts from this morning.

limitations: Death toll estimates vary widely depending on whether later radiation deaths are counted.
title: A nuclear weapon is used on Hiroshima
note: One bomb killed on the order of 70,000 to 140,000 people by the end of the year. It is the first of the only two uses of nuclear weapons in war, and the reference point for every threat made since.

limitations: Death toll estimates vary widely depending on whether later radiation deaths are counted.
title: A second nuclear weapon is used on Nagasaki
note: A second bomb killed on the order of 40,000 to 80,000 people, and Japan announced its surrender five days later. The two attacks are the whole empirical record of nuclear use against a city.

title: The Soviet Union enters the war against Japan
note: A Soviet offensive destroyed the Japanese army in Manchuria within days and removed the last hope in Tokyo of a negotiated end through Moscow. Historians still argue whether this or the bombs weighed more in the surrender.

title: Japan surrenders
note: The end date is not disputed. The start date still is.

title: The United Nations holds its first General Assembly
note: Fifty-one states met in London to open the body built to keep the peace after the world war. It gave small states a standing forum and gave the five permanent Security Council members a veto over enforcement.

title: The United States pledges to contain Soviet expansion
note: A message to Congress promised aid to Greece and Turkey and framed the world as a contest between two ways of life. It converted a regional aid request into an open-ended commitment to resist Soviet gains anywhere.

title: British India is partitioned into two states
note: Independence created India and Pakistan at once and left the status of Kashmir unsettled. The new border became one of the most persistent interstate rivalries of the following seventy years.

limitations: Death and displacement estimates vary widely across sources.
title: Partition displaces millions across the new border
note: Publication of the boundary award set off mass migration and communal killing in Punjab and Bengal. The displacement fixed grievances into both national stories and shaped the wars that followed.

title: Twenty-three states sign the first global tariff agreement
note: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade bound its signatories to cut tariffs and to treat each other's goods alike. It was built on the view that the trade wars of the 1930s had helped bring on the shooting war.

title: The United States funds European reconstruction
note: The European Recovery Program sent large-scale aid to sixteen western European economies over four years. Recovery removed the economic collapse that both sides expected would decide Europe's alignment.

title: Israel declares independence as the British mandate ends
note: The declaration was followed within a day by war with neighboring Arab states. The territorial questions left open in 1948 organized the region's interstate conflicts for decades.

title: The Soviet Union closes land access to West Berlin
note: Rail and road links to the western sectors were cut and supplies were flown in for almost a year. It was the first direct test of whether the two blocs would fight over Germany, and both chose pressure short of force.

title: Twelve states sign the North Atlantic Treaty
note: The treaty committed each signatory to treat an attack on one as an attack on all. It reduced the chance of a probe against a weak member and raised the number of states any European war would pull in.

title: The Soviet Union tests its first nuclear weapon
note: The test ended the American monopoly four years after Hiroshima. From this point a direct war between the two strongest states carried a risk neither could bound, which pushed their contest into third countries.

title: The Chinese civil war ends with a communist victory
note: The People's Republic was proclaimed in Beijing and the defeated government withdrew to Taiwan. It added a second large communist power to the system and left an unresolved sovereignty dispute across the strait.

title: North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel
note: The attack turned a divided peninsula into a conventional interstate war within days. A misread of how the United States would respond is the standard explanation for why the attack was attempted at all.

title: Chinese forces enter the Korean war
note: Chinese units crossed the Yalu after United Nations forces advanced toward the border. A theater war became a war between a nuclear power and a large continental army, and the front settled near where it started.

title: An armistice freezes the Korean front line
note: The agreement stopped the fighting without a peace treaty and set a demilitarized zone near the original division. It is the standard case of a war that ends in a stalemate rather than a settlement.

title: The French garrison at Dien Bien Phu surrenders
note: The defeat ended French rule in Indochina and led to a partition of Vietnam at the Geneva conference. The partition was meant to be temporary and instead became the line a second war was fought over.

limitations: Death toll estimates range widely between French and Algerian sources.
title: An armed independence campaign opens in Algeria
note: Coordinated attacks began a war that France treated as an internal matter because Algeria was administered as part of France. It ran eight years, brought down a French republic, and ended in independence.

limitations: Dated to the official notification month; the cause was confirmed years later.
title: Industrial mercury poisoning is identified in a Japanese bay
note: A factory discharge into coastal waters was traced to severe neurological illness in a fishing community. It became the standard case for how long a state and a firm can deny an environmental harm they can measure.

title: Three states attack Egypt over the Suez Canal
note: Israel, Britain and France moved against Egypt after the canal was nationalized, then withdrew under American and Soviet pressure. It showed that the older European powers could no longer run a war their patron opposed.

title: Soviet forces crush the Hungarian uprising
note: Armored columns entered Budapest and ended an attempt to leave the eastern bloc. Western governments did not intervene, which fixed the understanding that each bloc would police its own sphere.

title: The first artificial satellite reaches orbit
note: A Soviet launch put a small satellite in orbit and proved a rocket that could reach any point on earth. Space capability and long-range missile capability were the same capability, and both sides read it that way.

limitations: Dated to the start of the worst year; death toll estimates range from 15 to 45 million.
title: A policy-driven famine begins in China
note: Collectivization and forced grain procurement produced mass starvation over roughly three years. It is the clearest modern case of a famine caused by a government's own program rather than by war or drought alone.

limitations: Dated to the start of the year; the independence dates are spread through 1960.
title: Seventeen African states become independent in one year
note: Colonial rule ended across most of west and central Africa within twelve months. It roughly doubled the number of sovereign states in the region and left many of them with borders and institutions they had not chosen.

title: Soviet missiles are found in Cuba
note: Photographs of missile sites started thirteen days in which the two nuclear powers came closest to direct war. It ended in a quarantine and a private trade of missile withdrawals rather than a strike.

limitations: The second reported attack is now generally judged not to have occurred.
title: A reported naval clash opens the way to a US ground war
note: A second reported attack on American destroyers, later shown to be doubtful, produced a congressional resolution authorizing force. It is the standard case of contested information driving an irreversible decision.

title: Israel and its neighbors fight a six-day war
note: Israel struck first after weeks of mobilization and closed waterways, and took the Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank and the Golan. The territories captured became the issue that later wars and talks were about.

limitations: Famine death estimates range from several hundred thousand to two million.
title: Nigeria's secession war produces a blockade famine
note: A breakaway region in the southeast was besieged and cut off from food for over two years. Televised starvation created the modern humanitarian relief campaign and the argument over aid crossing a war line.

title: A coordinated offensive across South Vietnam
note: Attacks on cities and bases were repulsed at heavy cost to the attackers but broke the American public's belief that the war was being won. It is the standard case of a military defeat that is a political victory.

title: Warsaw Pact forces occupy Czechoslovakia
note: Half a million troops ended an attempt to liberalize a bloc member. The doctrine announced afterward claimed a right to intervene in any socialist state, which locked the eastern bloc in place for twenty years.

title: A crewed spacecraft lands on the moon
note: The landing settled the space race that had run since the first satellite. Prestige competition absorbed effort that both sides might otherwise have spent on weapons, and it ended without a shot.

title: The first message is sent between two networked computers
note: A defense-funded research network linked its first two nodes in California. The design that grew out of it became the medium through which later states would conduct sabotage and interference.

title: The nuclear non-proliferation treaty enters into force
note: States without nuclear weapons agreed not to acquire them in exchange for access to civil nuclear technology and a promise of eventual disarmament. Far fewer states built weapons than forecasts of the 1960s expected.

title: The United States ends dollar convertibility into gold
note: The move suspended the fixed exchange rate system built after the war and led to floating currencies. It removed a shared monetary anchor and made currency policy a recurring source of friction between allies.

title: India and Pakistan fight over East Pakistan
note: A crackdown and mass refugee flow into India were followed by open war and the creation of Bangladesh. It is the clearest case of a refugee crisis pulling a neighboring state into a war it might otherwise have avoided.

title: A US presidential visit reopens relations with China
note: The visit ended more than two decades without contact between the two governments. It split the two large communist powers into separate poles and changed the arithmetic of every later crisis in Asia.

title: Egypt and Syria attack Israeli-held territory
note: A surprise attack on a religious holiday recovered ground before being pushed back, and both superpowers moved to resupply their clients. The near-parity of the fighting made the later peace talks possible.

title: Arab oil producers embargo states backing Israel
note: Production cuts and a targeted embargo quadrupled the crude price within months. It proved that energy supply could be used as a direct instrument against militarily stronger states.

limitations: Death toll estimates range from 1.5 to 2 million.
title: A revolutionary government empties Cambodia's cities
note: Forced evacuation, executions and starvation killed a large share of the population over four years. It ended only when a neighboring state invaded, which is the rare case of a mass atrocity stopped by force.

title: Thirty-five states accept Europe's postwar borders
note: The final act traded western recognition of existing borders for eastern commitments on human rights. The human rights language gave dissident movements in the east a text their own governments had signed.

title: Iran's monarchy is replaced by a clerical republic
note: A mass movement removed a government that had been the main American partner in the Gulf. The new state's regional posture and the loss of its oil output reordered both the security and the energy map.

limitations: Dated to the first of the month; the price rise ran through 1979 and 1980.
title: Iranian output collapse doubles the oil price
note: Strikes and revolution cut Iranian production and buyers bid the price up far beyond the lost volume. The second shock in six years pushed western economies into recession and high interest rates.

title: Soviet forces enter Afghanistan
note: An intervention meant to secure a client government became a decade-long war against insurgents armed from outside. The cost is part of why the Soviet system could not sustain its commitments ten years later.

title: Smallpox is declared eradicated
note: A worldwide vaccination campaign run through the health assembly removed the disease from circulation. It was carried out across the bloc division and remains the clearest proof that rival states can finish a joint program.

title: A Polish strike wins the eastern bloc's first free trade union
note: An agreement signed at the Gdansk shipyard allowed an independent union with millions of members. It showed a bloc government conceding to organized labor rather than calling in Soviet troops.

title: Iraq invades Iran
note: An attack timed to a neighbor's revolutionary disorder became eight years of trench and missile warfare. Chemical weapons were used repeatedly and the war ended near the border where it began.

title: The first clinical reports of what becomes AIDS appear
note: A short public health notice described a cluster of rare infections in Los Angeles. The epidemic that followed killed tens of millions and became the first health crisis treated as a security question by states.

title: Argentina occupies the Falkland Islands
note: A junta under domestic pressure seized islands it claimed, and Britain retook them in ten weeks. It is the standard case of a leadership using an external claim to shore up its position at home and losing both.

limitations: Dated to the broadcast that triggered the international response; the famine ran from 1983.
title: Famine in Ethiopia reaches world attention
note: Drought combined with war and forced resettlement produced mass starvation in the north. Aid reached areas the government controlled far more easily than areas held by insurgents, which shaped who survived.

limitations: Immediate and long-term death toll estimates differ by an order of magnitude.
title: A pesticide plant releases toxic gas over an Indian city
note: A gas leak from a chemical works killed thousands within days and injured many times that number. It set the terms of the argument over what a foreign parent company owes when its subsidiary causes mass harm.

title: Five governments agree to push the dollar down
note: Finance ministers coordinated intervention to weaken the dollar against the yen and the mark. The sharp yen appreciation that followed is part of the chain that produced Japan's asset bubble.

limitations: Long-term mortality estimates remain contested.
title: A reactor explosion contaminates a wide area of Europe
note: A test at a Ukrainian power station destroyed the reactor and spread fallout across the continent. The initial concealment damaged the Soviet government's standing at home more than the accident damaged its economy.

title: States agree to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals
note: The protocol set binding cuts with a fund to help poorer states comply and has been ratified by every state. It is the working example of an environmental agreement that changed industrial behavior.

limitations: Death toll estimates range from several hundred to several thousand.
title: China's army clears protesters from the capital's central square
note: Weeks of demonstrations ended when troops moved in overnight. The Chinese leadership drew the opposite lesson from the one drawn in eastern Europe that year, and the party's hold was not loosened.

title: The Berlin Wall is opened
note: Border crossings were opened after weeks of protest and the eastern bloc's division of Germany ended within a year. No shots were fired, which is the striking part of how the European standoff came apart.

title: Japan's stock market reaches its peak
note: The index closed at a record and then fell for most of the following two decades. The stagnation removed the state most often named in the 1980s as the coming challenger to American economic primacy.

title: Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait
note: A debt and oil dispute ended in the outright absorption of a neighboring state. Erasing a United Nations member produced a coalition that neither side had expected to form.

title: A coalition drives Iraqi forces out of Kuwait
note: An air campaign followed by a short ground war restored the border and left the Iraqi government in place. The coalition acted with Security Council authorization, which had not been possible during the bloc division.

title: Yugoslavia begins to break apart in war
note: Fighting followed declarations of independence by two republics and spread over the next four years. A federal state dissolving without an agreed rule for who inherits what is a recurring path into war.

title: The World Wide Web is opened to the public
note: A hypertext system built at a physics laboratory was posted for anyone to use. It became the layer on which information operations, propaganda and financial contagion later moved at the speed they now do.

title: The Soviet Union is dissolved
note: Fifteen republics became independent states and the second superpower stopped existing. The nuclear arsenal, the borders and the minority populations left behind became the material of the next three decades of disputes.

title: European states sign the treaty creating the European Union
note: The treaty set up a political union and the path to a single currency. Tying reunified Germany into a deeper union was an explicit answer to the question of how to hold Europe together after the bloc division ended.

title: A genocide in Rwanda kills roughly 800,000 people in a hundred days
note: Organized killing began the day after the president's aircraft was shot down and ran until an insurgent force took the country. The peacekeeping mission present was cut rather than reinforced.

title: South Africa holds its first universal election
note: Voting open to all adults ended minority rule after four decades of formal segregation. A transition many observers expected to end in civil war was settled by negotiation instead.

title: More than 8,000 people are killed at a declared safe area
note: A United Nations protected enclave was overrun and its men and boys were killed. The failure of the protection promise is the reason later interventions were argued on the ground of preventing atrocity.

title: A negotiated settlement ends the Bosnian war
note: The agreement kept a single state with two internal entities and put a large armed force behind it. It is the standard case of a war ended by outside powers imposing a settlement neither side would have reached alone.

title: A currency collapse in Thailand spreads across Asia
note: The Thai baht was floated and capital fled the region, forcing bailouts and deep recessions. The political fallout brought down governments and left several states determined never to depend on outside lenders again.

title: The first binding emissions treaty is adopted
note: Industrialized states accepted targets while developing states did not, and the largest emitter never ratified. It set the pattern of climate agreements that are hard to enforce against the states that matter most.

title: Russia devalues and defaults on domestic debt
note: The government abandoned its currency band and stopped paying on short-term bonds. The collapse discredited the reform program of the 1990s and set the conditions for the centralized state that followed.

title: An alliance bombs Yugoslavia over Kosovo
note: The campaign ran eleven weeks without Security Council authorization and ended with the province under international administration. It is the case both sides in later disputes cite about when force is legitimate.

title: India and Pakistan fight in Kashmir after both test nuclear weapons
note: Regular forces fought over occupied heights a year after both states declared themselves nuclear powers. It showed that nuclear weapons did not stop a limited conventional war between the two.

title: Coordinated attacks kill nearly 3,000 people in the United States
note: Hijacked aircraft struck buildings in New York and near Washington. A non-state group inflicted a scale of damage previously associated with states, and the response reorganized alliances for a decade.

title: A US-led campaign begins in Afghanistan
note: Air strikes and allied ground forces removed the governing movement within weeks. The alliance invoked its mutual defense clause for the first time, over an attack by a non-state group.

title: China joins the World Trade Organization
note: Accession locked in tariff cuts and opened western markets to Chinese manufacturing. It is the single decision most often cited in later arguments about industrial decline and about how a power transition was financed.

title: A global alert is issued for a new respiratory virus
note: The health assembly issued its first worldwide alert in over a decade after cases spread from southern China. Delayed reporting by one government became the case used to rewrite the international health regulations.

title: A coalition invades Iraq
note: The invasion went ahead without Security Council authorization and on intelligence about weapons that was not borne out. The occupation that followed produced an insurgency and a long sectarian war.

limitations: Death toll estimates range from under 100,000 to over 300,000.
title: War in Darfur displaces millions
note: Insurgent attacks were answered by a government-backed militia campaign against civilian populations. It became the first conflict a major government formally labeled genocide while it was still going on.

title: Ten states join the European Union
note: Eight former eastern bloc states plus two Mediterranean islands joined at once. The expansion moved the union's border to the edge of the former Soviet Union and became a standing grievance in Moscow.

title: An undersea earthquake kills more than 220,000 people
note: Waves crossed the Indian Ocean and struck fourteen countries with no warning system in place. In Indonesia the relief operation helped end a thirty-year separatist war, while in Sri Lanka it did not.

title: A cross-border raid starts a month-long war in Lebanon
note: A militia raid and abduction were answered with air strikes and a ground incursion, and rocket fire reached Israeli cities. It is a clear case of a state fighting a war against an armed group inside a neighboring state.

title: Russia and Georgia fight a five-day war
note: Fighting in South Ossetia brought Russian forces deep into Georgia and ended with recognition of two breakaway regions. It was the first time since 1991 that Russia used force to change a neighbor's borders.

title: A large investment bank fails and credit markets freeze
note: The bankruptcy turned a housing downturn into a worldwide financial crisis and a deep recession. The loss of confidence in western economic management is part of why the following decade's politics turned inward.

limitations: Civilian death toll in the final months is disputed and estimates range widely.
title: Sri Lanka's civil war ends in a military victory
note: A twenty-six-year insurgency was destroyed in a final offensive with heavy civilian casualties in the last enclave. It is the case most often cited by governments arguing that insurgencies can be defeated outright.

title: A new influenza strain is declared a pandemic
note: The health assembly raised its alert to the top level for the first time under the revised regulations. Vaccine supply went to the states that had signed advance contracts, which set the pattern later repeated.

title: Malware built to damage industrial equipment is discovered
note: A worm designed to destroy uranium enrichment centrifuges was found on systems outside its target. It is the first widely documented case of code used to cause physical damage in place of an air strike.

title: Uprising in Syria becomes a civil war
note: Within four years Russia, Iran, Turkey, the Gulf states and the United States all have forces or proxies inside one country.

title: NATO intervention in Libya begins
note: The intervention that Moscow later cites as proof that a UN mandate can be stretched into regime change.

title: Russia annexes Crimea
note: The first forcible annexation in Europe since 1945. Sanctions follow; the border war in the Donbas never stops.

title: Saudi-led coalition intervenes in Yemen
note: A civil war becomes a proxy war between Riyadh and Tehran, with American support on one side.

title: Russia intervenes in Syria
note: Russian and American aircraft share Syrian airspace with a deconfliction hotline. The first theater where the two operate at arm's length.

title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh war
note: Six weeks, decided by drones. Turkey backs one side, Russia brokers the ceasefire, and the settlement is undone three years later.

title: Coup in Myanmar; civil war follows
note: One of the deadliest conflicts of the decade and the least connected to the others. It is on the map to show that not everything links.

title: Russia invades Ukraine
note: The largest interstate war in Europe since 1945. Planned as a short campaign; in its fifth year as of this page's date.

title: Iranian-designed drones strike Kyiv
note: The first hard connection between the Gulf and Europe: one theater's weapons in another theater's sky.

title: War between Sudan's army and the RSF
note: The world's largest displacement crisis, armed from the Gulf on both sides.

title: Hamas attack; the Gaza war begins
note: Within weeks the war has fronts in Lebanon, the Red Sea, Iraq and Syria.

title: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping begin
note: A war in Gaza reroutes global trade around Africa. American and European navies join a second front.

title: Iran's first direct strike on Israel
note: Decades of proxy war become direct fire between states. Telegraphed in advance, mostly intercepted, and a step that cannot be untaken.

title: North Korean troops reported in Russia
note: Soldiers from one theater-in-waiting fighting in another. The first time since 1953 that North Korean forces fight abroad.

title: The Syrian government falls
note: Russia, committed in Ukraine, and Iran, weakened by a year of Israeli strikes, cannot save their client. One theater's outcome is decided by two others.

title: India strikes Pakistan after the Pahalgam attack
note: Four days of missile and drone exchanges between two nuclear states. Chinese aircraft and Western aircraft meet in combat for the first time.

title: Israel strikes Iran; the twelve-day war
note: A preventive war against a nuclear program, launched during negotiations.

title: The United States bombs three Iranian nuclear sites
note: The first direct American strike on Iranian soil. A ceasefire follows within days.

title: U.S. operation captures Venezuelan president
note: U.S. forces captured Nicolas Maduro and his wife in Venezuela. Trump said Washington would oversee a transition.
effects: Venezuelan leadership was removed by an external military operation.
implication: Intervention links sovereignty disputes, regime change and resource interests; it can alter other states' expectations about the use of force.
limitations: The U.S. statement about running Venezuela was an announced intention, not proof of complete administrative control.

title: UN expert challenges legitimacy of Myanmar election
note: A UN expert criticized the military-organized election and exclusion of major opposition forces, including the National League for Democracy.
effects: The assessment disputed the election's claim to political legitimacy.
implication: Excluding opponents can weaken peaceful bargaining and prolong incentives for armed resistance.
limitations: This is an attributed UN expert assessment. Voting began in 2025; the recorded event is the January 2026 assessment.

title: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of supplying rebels
note: Ethiopian police alleged Eritrean support for rebels and reported an ammunition seizure in Amhara.
effects: The allegation intensified a diplomatic feud between the neighboring states.
implication: Alleged external support for insurgents can connect civil conflict to interstate confrontation.
limitations: External sponsorship is an allegation attributed to Ethiopian authorities, not independently established here.

title: EU and Mercosur sign partnership and trade agreements
note: The European Union and Mercosur signed a partnership agreement and an interim trade agreement.
effects: The agreements formalized closer interregional economic and political ties.
implication: Trade diversification can strengthen cooperation while reducing dependence on individual large markets.
limitations: Signature is distinct from ratification and entry into force. The Commission records provisional application of the interim agreement from May 1.

title: U.S. threatens tariffs over Greenland
note: Trump threatened additional tariffs on eight European states in connection with his demand to acquire Greenland.
effects: An additional 10 percent tariff was proposed for February 1. The dispute placed economic pressure on NATO allies over territorial sovereignty.
implication: Economic coercion within an alliance can weaken trust and complicate collective deterrence.
limitations: Threatened tariffs were subsequently withdrawn on January 21; do not count them as implemented.

title: U.S. withdraws Greenland-linked tariff threat
note: Following a meeting with NATO's secretary general, Trump withdrew the tariffs scheduled for February 1 and described a framework for further talks.
effects: The announced additional tariff shock was averted at that point. The reversal reduced immediate friction with European allies.
implication: This is evidence of bargaining and restraint within an escalating dispute.
limitations: A framework announcement did not settle Greenland's sovereignty or eliminate the broader dispute.

title: Colombia suspends electricity sales during tariff dispute
note: Colombia announced tariffs on selected Ecuadorian goods and suspended electricity exports after Ecuador's tariff announcement.
effects: Electricity trade was interrupted; Colombia announced 30 percent tariffs on 20 products. Border-security accusations became a bilateral trade dispute.
implication: Interdependence can become a coercive instrument when energy supply and security accusations are linked.
limitations: Colombia also cited domestic electricity-supply protection; the interruption should not be assigned a single motive.

title: EU and India conclude trade negotiations and sign security partnership
note: The summit concluded free-trade negotiations and signed an EU-India security and defence partnership.
effects: The parties expanded their strategic relationship.
implication: Cooperation across trade and security diversifies partnerships; it does not establish a mutual-defence alliance.
limitations: Conclusion of negotiations does not mean the trade agreement was already in force.

title: Syrian government and Kurdish-led forces agree integration framework
note: Damascus and the SDF announced a ceasefire and phased integration of military and governing structures.
effects: The agreement proposed incorporating Kurdish-led institutions into the Syrian state.
implication: Integration can reduce fragmentation, but implementation depends on credible protection and security commitments.
limitations: Agreement does not establish completed integration or a durable nationwide peace.

title: New START expires
note: The bilateral strategic nuclear arms-limitation treaty expired in February 2026.
effects: Its treaty-based numerical framework ceased to bind the two states.
implication: Reduced predictability about future arsenals can intensify worst-case planning and arms competition.
limitations: Expiry does not itself demonstrate an immediate increase in deployed warheads. Inspections and implementation had already been disrupted before 2026.

title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects emergency-law global tariffs
note: The Supreme Court struck down the administration's sweeping tariffs imposed under an emergency-powers law.
effects: The ruling affected major import duties and created refund and policy questions. The judiciary constrained this use of presidential economic authority.
implication: Institutional checks can limit coercive policy, although governments may pursue alternative legal instruments.
limitations: The ruling did not abolish all U.S. tariffs or prevent replacement measures under other authorities.

title: Somalia hunger assessment warns of severe deterioration
note: The government and UN agencies warned that nearly 6.5 million people faced high levels of hunger amid worsening drought.
effects: More than 1.8 million children faced acute malnutrition, according to the assessment.
implication: Food stress can compound displacement and state fragility; it is not evidence that interstate war is inevitable.
metricName: People facing high levels of hunger
limitations: Assessment figures are estimates; hunger and child-malnutrition populations overlap and must not be added.

title: Pakistan strikes Afghanistan as cross-border conflict intensifies
note: Pakistan conducted air and ground strikes inside Afghanistan. Taliban authorities indicated willingness to negotiate.
effects: Pakistan's defence minister described the confrontation as open war.
implication: Cross-border militant disputes can escalate into direct interstate fighting even while negotiations remain possible.
limitations: Both sides issued conflicting casualty claims; no combined toll is adopted here.

title: U.S. launches Operation Epic Fury against Iran
note: CENTCOM announced the start of a campaign against Iranian military targets on February 28.
effects: The operation established direct U.S. participation in the new campaign against Iran.
implication: Direct intervention raises risks of retaliation against bases, partners and maritime routes.
limitations: CENTCOM is a belligerent source. Its claims about imminent threats or operational success are not independently adopted.

title: France announces expanded nuclear deterrence policy
note: Macron announced an increase in France's nuclear arsenal and an end to public disclosure of its size.
effects: France advanced discussions on a broader European role for its deterrent.
implication: The policy combines deterrence reassurance with reduced transparency and possible arms-race effects.
limitations: An announced increase is not a verified count of newly produced or deployed warheads.

title: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz
note: A fifth of the world's oil trade is held hostage to the bargaining. The war's cost spreads to every economy.

title: UNCTAD warns of Hormuz trade spillovers
note: UNCTAD identified risks from shipping disruptions to energy, fertilizers and vulnerable economies.
effects: The assessment linked the disruption to commodity-market and transport exposure.
implication: A regional chokepoint can transmit costs to distant food systems and import-dependent economies.
limitations: The assessment describes exposure and risks; it does not measure every country's realized loss.

title: IEA members agree record emergency oil-stock release
note: IEA members unanimously agreed to make 400 million barrels of emergency oil available in response to Middle East disruptions.
effects: The announcement provided a coordinated buffer against interrupted supply.
implication: Emergency stocks can soften a shock, but repeated drawdowns reduce future cushioning capacity.
limitations: Agreed availability is not the same as barrels already delivered to the market.

title: EU strengthens coordinated response to hybrid threats
note: The Council adopted conclusions on countering hybrid campaigns and condemned Russian and proxy activity.
effects: The policy reaffirmed coordinated use of the EU's hybrid and cyber-diplomacy instruments.
implication: Sabotage and information operations can erode trust below the threshold of sustained open warfare.
limitations: The Council's attribution is an official position; the policy release is not a catalogue independently verifying each alleged incident.

title: WFP models additional hunger from prolonged Middle East war
note: WFP estimated almost 45 million additional people could enter acute food insecurity if fighting persisted to midyear and oil stayed above USD 100.
implication: Fuel and transport shocks can magnify humanitarian pressures far from the battlefield.
metricName: Additional people at risk under scenario
limitations: Conditional March forecast, not an observed September count. The scenario conditions and later outcomes must be checked separately.

title: Freedom House reports twentieth consecutive annual freedom decline
note: The 2026 report assessed 2025: 54 countries deteriorated in rights and liberties, while 35 improved.
effects: The assessment identified continued global erosion of political freedoms.
implication: Weaker accountability can affect leaders' incentives and information quality, but this index is not a war predictor.
limitations: Published in 2026 but measures 2025. Freedom House uses its own normative scoring methodology.

title: WTO forecasts slower trade with downside from energy shocks
note: WTO forecast 1.9 percent merchandise-trade growth in its baseline and 1.4 percent in a sustained high-energy-price scenario.
effects: The baseline excluded the modeled energy-price shock.
implication: Lower trade growth narrows economic gains from cooperation and raises pressure on import-dependent states.
limitations: Forecasts are scenario-dependent, not realized annual growth. WTO and IMF global-growth measures are not interchangeable.

title: U.S. agencies warn of Iranian-affiliated attacks on industrial controllers
note: A joint advisory described exploitation of programmable logic controllers across U.S. critical infrastructure.
effects: Some victims experienced operational disruption and financial loss, according to the advisory.
implication: Cyber operations can extend conflict into civilian infrastructure without conventional attacks on U.S. territory.

source.label: FBI; CISA; NSA; EPA; DOE; USCYBERCOM

limitations: Attribution is the agencies' assessment. The advisory does not establish that every targeted organization suffered disruption.

title: IMF revises outlook under Middle East war shock
note: The April outlook projected global growth of 3.1 percent in 2026 under an assumption of limited conflict.
effects: The IMF identified higher commodity prices, inflation pressure and tighter financial conditions.
implication: A prolonged shock could reduce fiscal room and intensify distributional disputes within importing countries.
limitations: April forecast vintage; superseded by later forecasts and not a realized annual result.

title: IMF warns of rising public debt and spending pressures
note: The Fiscal Monitor estimated global public debt just below 94 percent of GDP in 2025 and projected 100 percent by 2029.
effects: Defence, social spending and interest costs were identified as pressures on public finances.
implication: High debt can limit responses to energy and security shocks and sharpen budget trade-offs.
metricName: Global public debt relative to GDP
limitations: The 2025 estimate and 2029 forecast are distinct; this row records their April 2026 publication.

title: Australia and Japan sign major frigate contracts
note: The countries signed contracts initiating a warship program valued at about AUD 10 billion.
effects: The program allocates shipbuilding work to Japan and Australia. The deal deepened bilateral defence-industrial cooperation.
implication: Expanded naval capability supports deterrence but can also reinforce competitive military planning.
limitations: Program value is not 2026 expenditure; deliveries are scheduled for later years.

title: EU adopts twentieth Russia sanctions package
note: The Council adopted additional restrictions targeting energy, the military-industrial sector, trade and financial services.
effects: Measures included 36 energy-sector designations. The package extended economic pressure over Russia's war against Ukraine.
implication: Sanctions seek to constrain war resources but can encourage trade rerouting and alternative financial channels.
limitations: Designations are not a measure of revenue lost or sanctions effectiveness.

title: Coordinated insurgent attacks hit Malian army positions
note: Large attacks targeted positions near Bamako and in northern cities; al-Qaeda-linked militants claimed responsibility.
effects: The attacks challenged the military authorities' security control.
implication: Coordinated attacks across distant sites indicate pressure on state capacity and raise risks to transport and economic activity.
limitations: The army's claimed assailant deaths are not treated as independently verified casualties.

title: SIPRI reports another annual increase in world military spending
note: SIPRI estimated 2025 military expenditure at USD 2,887 billion, a 2.9 percent real increase and the eleventh successive annual rise.
effects: The release measures resources devoted to military activity.
implication: Persistent rearmament can reflect both deterrence needs and reinforcing arms competition.
limitations: These are 2025 spending estimates published in April 2026, not 2026 spending. The dollar total and real growth rate use different measurement conventions.

title: World Bank forecasts sharp rise in energy prices
note: The Commodity Markets Outlook projected energy prices to rise 24 percent in 2026 and overall commodity prices 16 percent.
effects: The outlook connected the forecasts to the Middle East supply shock.
implication: The same price rise can benefit exporters while worsening inflation, external balances and subsidies for importers.
limitations: Forecast as of April 28; not a September spot price or realized full-year inflation rate.

title: Fighting damages health infrastructure in Jonglei
note: OCHA reported at least 33 health facilities destroyed, looted or damaged in conflict-affected Jonglei areas.
effects: The damage reduced access to health services.
implication: Loss of basic services deepens displacement pressures and weakens the capacity to stabilize conflict-affected communities.
metricName: Health facilities destroyed, looted or damaged
limitations: The count spans the report's cumulative conflict context, not necessarily incidents occurring only during April 18-30.

title: Ecuador-Colombia tariff dispute escalates
note: Ecuador's announced 100 percent tariff took effect; Colombia formalized differentiated retaliatory rates on about 190 products.
effects: Business groups reported a collapse in bilateral trade. The dispute further strained bilateral relations.
implication: Reciprocal tariff escalation can amplify domestic pressure while reducing incentives for cooperative border management.
limitations: Reuters noted uncertainty about the products covered by Ecuador's measure; do not apply this rate to every transaction.

title: EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement begins provisional application
note: The European Commission records provisional application of the interim trade agreement from May 1.
effects: The trade framework began operating provisionally.
implication: Rules-based trade integration is a counter-indicator to a narrative of universal economic fragmentation.
limitations: Provisional application of the interim agreement is different from full ratification of the broader partnership agreement.

title: Thailand and Cambodia commit to trust-building measures
note: Leaders met at an ASEAN gathering and agreed to pursue trust-building and normalization after the previous year's border fighting.
effects: The meeting supported an existing fragile ceasefire.
implication: Regional mediation and communication can reduce misperception around contested borders.
limitations: The meeting did not resolve every boundary issue or establish that displaced people could safely return.

title: UN experts warn of humanitarian effects of Cuba fuel restrictions
note: UN experts criticized U.S. measures threatening tariffs on countries supplying Cuba with oil.
effects: The experts linked fuel restrictions to severe development pressures. They warned of serious human-rights consequences.
implication: Energy coercion can transmit political pressure through civilian services and livelihoods.
limitations: This row records the May assessment of measures initiated in January; it does not assign every Cuban economic problem to those measures.

title: Taiwan responds to U.S.-China summit
note: Taiwan said the Trump-Xi summit produced no surprises and urged China to stop military pressure. Xi warned of conflict risks over Taiwan.
effects: High-level U.S.-China dialogue continued alongside unresolved sovereignty tensions.
implication: Leader-level contact can support crisis management without resolving the underlying commitment and sovereignty disputes.
limitations: Dialogue is not a security guarantee, a peace treaty or evidence that military pressure ended.

title: NPT review conference ends without consensus
note: The review conference ended without an agreed consensus outcome after four weeks of negotiations.
effects: States failed to agree on a common review document.
implication: Failure to agree weakens a diplomatic channel for addressing disarmament and non-proliferation disputes.
limitations: Failure of a review conference does not terminate the NPT or establish that all states have abandoned their treaty obligations.

title: WMO urges preparation for El Nino
note: WMO forecast an 80 percent likelihood of El Nino during June-August 2026.
implication: Seasonal climate risks can compound food and energy shocks, particularly where conflict already limits adaptation.
limitations: A climate probability is not a probability of war; regional effects vary and later forecasts supersede this vintage.

title: SIPRI publishes January 2026 nuclear inventory estimates
note: SIPRI estimated 12,187 total warheads, including about 9,745 in military stockpiles and 4,012 deployed.
effects: The report warned of increasing reliance on nuclear weapons and reduced transparency.
implication: Inventory and alert posture affect potential escalation consequences; they do not demonstrate that nuclear use is imminent.
limitations: Total inventory includes retired warheads awaiting dismantlement; it is not the deployed-warhead count.

title: UCDP reports record state-based conflict count for 2025
note: UCDP recorded 65 state-based conflicts in 2025, including eight interstate conflicts and thirteen conflicts reaching war intensity.
effects: The release documented a rise in interstate conflict within its dataset.
implication: The figures provide background to 2026 escalation concerns but cannot establish a single connected world war.
limitations: 2026 publication of 2025 data. Interstate conflicts and war-intensity conflicts are different classifications and should not be added.

title: UNHCR publishes global forced-displacement baseline
note: UNHCR reported 117.8 million forcibly displaced people worldwide at the end of 2025.
effects: The figure describes a large population requiring protection and support.
implication: Displacement affects host-country services and politics, but responses depend on institutions and policy choices.
limitations: A stock of displaced people, not new displacement during 2026 or a death toll.

title: Islamabad Memorandum ends the war on paper
note: Blockades lifted on both sides. A settlement each side prefers to fighting, which is what the theory predicts should exist.

title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire announced with international mediation
note: A senior U.S. official said Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a ceasefire negotiated with U.S., Qatari and Iranian involvement.
effects: The agreement created a pause in a linked regional conflict.
implication: Mediation involving different partners can interrupt escalation across connected theaters.
limitations: Attributed to a U.S. official. A ceasefire announcement is not proof of permanent compliance or a political settlement.

title: Gaza health report describes dialysis-treatment shortages
note: OCHA reported a shortage of therapeutic erythropoietin affecting dialysis care.
effects: More patients required blood transfusions, adding pressure to blood supplies and hospital capacity.
implication: Prolonged disruption to medical supply systems creates harm extending beyond immediately recorded battle casualties.
limitations: The shortage began before 2026. This row records its documented persistence, not a new June onset.

title: IMF July update combines weaker growth and renewed inflation pressure
note: The IMF projected 3.0 percent global growth and 4.7 percent headline inflation for 2026.
effects: The outlook described diverging effects across energy exporters, technology-linked economies and vulnerable importers.
implication: The shock is uneven; a global average can conceal large differences in national resilience.
limitations: July forecast vintage; not actual 2026 growth. Inflation and growth are separate measures.

title: NATO announces new procurement and manufacturing commitments
note: The Ankara declaration announced more than USD 50 billion in new procurements and expanded collective manufacturing commitments.
effects: The commitments support defence production and industrial capacity. Allies reaffirmed a combined nuclear, conventional, missile, cyber and space posture.
implication: Capacity building can strengthen deterrence and create reciprocal threat perceptions.
limitations: Commitments are not equivalent to completed deliveries, annual spending or a declaration of war.

title: Ceasefire collapses over shipping in Hormuz
note: The deal could not be enforced. The textbook commitment problem, three weeks after the signature.

title: China and Philippines summon envoys after maritime encounter
note: The two governments summoned each other's representatives following a disputed South China Sea encounter.
effects: The parties issued conflicting accounts of responsibility.
implication: Repeated maritime encounters can create miscalculation and alliance-entanglement risks.
limitations: Descriptions of ramming and attacks are disputed allegations; no finding of responsibility is made.

title: IEA reports substantial emergency-stock drawdown
note: The IEA reported 290 million barrels released since the March collective action.
effects: Emergency inventories had supplied the market during prolonged disruption.
implication: Drawdowns cushion current scarcity but reduce stocks available for subsequent shocks.
limitations: Cumulative reported release is distinct from the original 400-million-barrel availability commitment.

title: Ukraine alleges plans for additional North Korean deployment
note: Zelenskiy said Russia intended to bring in 30,000 North Korean troops and was preparing to receive them.
effects: The statement highlighted potential expansion of external participation in the war.
implication: Additional foreign forces could deepen links between European and East Asian security dynamics.
metricName: Additional deployment alleged by Ukrainian president
limitations: This is a claimed future plan, not a verified count of arrivals. See the August 24 assessment for qualification.

title: Displacement persists after Cambodia-Thailand fighting
note: A UN expert reported more than 20,000 Cambodian civilians still displaced along the Thai border.
effects: Displacement continued despite a bilateral ceasefire.
implication: A pause in fighting may leave unresolved security and livelihood barriers to return.
limitations: The displacement followed fighting in 2025; it is not a count of people newly displaced during July 2026.

title: Ceasefire monitors deploy in eastern Congo
note: Monitors deployed following a renewed roadmap for negotiations between the government and AFC/M23.
effects: The Doha process ran alongside U.S.-mediated Congo-Rwanda talks.
implication: Monitoring may improve information and compliance; parallel mediation tracks require coordination.
limitations: Deployment does not prove an end to fighting. Hoped-for mining investment is not recorded as a realized economic gain.

title: South Korean assessment qualifies imminent-deployment claims
note: A lawmaker's office reported preparations for further North Korean deployments but no sign that a deployment was imminent.
effects: The assessment distinguished preparation from an immediate movement of troops.
implication: This qualifies earlier escalation claims and illustrates uncertainty about partners' military intentions.
limitations: An attributed intelligence-related assessment is not independent verification of either deployment timing or troop numbers.

title: Taiwan warns of growing Chinese air and sea control
note: Taiwan described expanding Chinese military pressure nearby while the U.S. continued arms support and ambiguity about intervention.
effects: The assessment underscored unresolved cross-strait security tensions.
implication: Persistent pressure can shorten perceived decision time without constituting an invasion.
limitations: The account is Taiwan's assessment. The row does not claim that a Chinese invasion or U.S.-China war had begun.

title: U.S. reports renewed strikes on IRGC targets
note: CENTCOM released video and a statement reporting strikes on IRGC targets in Iran.
effects: The release documented continued direct U.S. combat participation.
implication: Repeated strikes create further opportunities for retaliation and maritime spillover.
limitations: Belligerent-source account; damage and military effectiveness are not independently quantified.

title: Iran strikes US bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq
note: The heaviest exchange in more than a month. Third countries are hit because the bases are there.

title: Observed Hormuz commodity-vessel transits fall sharply
note: Kpler data reported by Reuters recorded four commodity vessels crossing on September 3, below a ten-day average of fifteen.
effects: The count indicated constrained observable commercial movement through the chokepoint.
implication: Persistent shipping restrictions can raise transport costs and disrupt access to energy and inputs.
limitations: The count excludes vessels with tracking transponders disabled and is not a count of all vessel types.

title: UN investigation links foreign networks and drones to Sudan war
note: UN investigators described foreign supply networks and more than 1,000 drone-attack deaths in the first half of 2026.
effects: The report identified civilian harm and possible war crimes.
implication: External financing, personnel and weapons can prolong civil wars and connect them to wider rivalries.
metricName: Deaths in drone attacks reported by investigators
limitations: Named countries are associated with alleged networks, not all proven state sponsors. Relevant governments denied allegations; possible war crimes are not court judgments.

title: WMO forecasts persistent and potentially very strong El Nino
note: WMO reported a near-certain likelihood that El Nino would persist through February 2027 and warned of extreme-weather risks.
implication: Climate shocks may interact with disrupted trade and food systems; effects vary substantially by region.
limitations: The probability concerns El Nino persistence, not a particular disaster or armed conflict.

title: FAO reports higher August food commodity prices
note: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 in August, rising 1.9 percent month-on-month and 2.5 percent year-on-year.
effects: FAO cited weather risks, conflict and disrupted trade logistics.
implication: Higher international food prices can worsen purchasing-power pressures where incomes and safety nets are weak.
limitations: International commodity index, not national grocery-price inflation. Weather and trade factors prevent attribution to war alone.

title: U.S. reports strikes on three Iranian oil carriers
note: CENTCOM said it struck three Iranian crude-oil carriers after Iran targeted two U.S. Navy warships.
effects: Oil-shipping assets were directly targeted.
implication: Attacks on vessels link military confrontation to energy export capacity and navigation risk.
metricName: Oil carriers struck according to CENTCOM
limitations: The sequence, vessel affiliation and damage description are attributed to CENTCOM.

title: France announces planned restrictions on settlement products
note: France announced plans to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
effects: The government cited settlement expansion and threats to a two-state solution; EU-wide agreement remained difficult.
implication: Economic restrictions show diplomatic fragmentation around the conflict without establishing military participation.
limitations: Implementation timing and detailed coverage were not settled in the cited report; this was not a blanket ban on Israeli goods.

title: Germany announces additional Patriot interceptors for Ukraine
note: Germany announced urgent transfers of additional Patriot PAC-2 interceptors from national stocks.
effects: The announcement responded to concerns about intensified attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.
implication: Air-defence support can protect civilians while drawing on finite donor inventories and linking allied defence planning.
limitations: An announcement is not proof of delivery. No unsupported missile quantity is assigned.

title: Haiti assessment documents large-scale displacement and hunger
note: The IRC's updated assessment reported nearly 1.5 million displaced people and about 5.8 million people lacking enough food.
effects: Displacement, hunger and insecurity remained widespread.
implication: Armed-group control and weak services can generate regional humanitarian and migration pressures without becoming interstate war.
limitations: Cumulative stock estimate. The displacement and hunger populations overlap and must not be added.

title: Houthi attacks hit Saudi cities and energy facilities
note: Saudi authorities reported Houthi attacks on cities and energy facilities, injuring 73 people.
effects: Authorities reported fires and operational interruptions. The coalition pledged a response.
implication: The attacks expand pressure on regional energy infrastructure and create further retaliation risks.
metricName: People injured according to Saudi authorities
limitations: Preliminary official injury count. Iran's relationship with the Houthis does not establish its direction of this specific attack.

title: Oil rises after Saudi energy-site attacks
note: Reuters reported Brent at USD 97.70 per barrel during trading following the attacks.
effects: Oil reached a six-week high amid renewed supply concerns.
implication: Importers face inflation and external-balance pressure while some exporters gain revenue; impacts are uneven.
limitations: Intraday quote, not a final daily close; prices may change after publication.

title: Russian strikes resume after temporary pause for U.S. envoys
note: Russia resumed attacks on Kyiv after the envoys' visit; Ukrainian authorities reported five deaths and nearly thirty injuries.
effects: Residential and public infrastructure were hit, according to the report.
implication: A temporary diplomatic pause did not establish a durable ceasefire or resolve bargaining disputes.
limitations: Casualty reports may be revised. The figure is not a nationwide or cumulative war toll.

title: U.S. expands sanctions targeting Iranian aviation networks
note: The United States announced 36 sanctions targets associated with Iran's aviation sector and procurement networks.
effects: Restrictions targeted access to aircraft, technology and financial channels. The action extended economic pressure during ongoing hostilities.
implication: Sanctions internationalize compliance pressures but do not make every affected country a belligerent.
limitations: Targeted entities and alleged activities are identified by U.S. authorities; effectiveness and losses are not quantified.

title: U.S. explores wider access to Venezuelan minerals
note: Reuters reported U.S. efforts to expand access to Venezuelan minerals after the January intervention.
effects: Officials were exploring investment and procurement opportunities. The initiative was linked to strategic competition with China.
implication: Resource access and intervention can become intertwined in perceptions of great-power intentions.
limitations: Possible executive action and investor interest are not completed projects or verified reserve valuations.

title: Ukraine reports promising ideas from renewed U.S. mediation
note: Zelenskiy described proposals from U.S. envoys positively after visits to Kyiv and Moscow, while no breakthrough was reported.
effects: Diplomatic engagement continued despite ongoing fighting.
implication: Continued negotiations are evidence that bargaining channels remain open, not proof that a settlement is near.
limitations: Proposed future summits and meetings are not treated as completed events.

title: UNCTAD warns Hormuz disruption threatens smaller businesses
note: UNCTAD warned that smaller firms were disproportionately exposed to Hormuz-related disruption.
effects: The agency identified risks of exclusion from global supply chains and greater market concentration.
implication: Unequal ability to absorb shipping shocks can concentrate economic power and weaken supply-chain resilience.
